subject: Operationalizing support access & break-glass — Acadia Health follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Park <emma.park@acadiahealth.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T15:02:00Z
Subject: Operationalizing support access & break-glass — Acadia Health follow-up

Hi Emma / Tom —

Quick recap from today's discovery and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: thanks for the time. High-level asks we captured:

- Data residency: Acadia requires customer data to remain in US regions only (no EU/APAC replication).
- PII handling: telemetry and API logs that may contain patient-identifying fields should be redacted in downstream analytics; you requested a short retention window for raw logs (90 days) and longer aggregated metrics.
- Support access: you prefer just-in-time (JIT) privileged access with manager approval, short-lived credentials, and an auditable break-glass workflow for emergency incidents.
- Audit/logging: Immutable audit trails for who accessed customer data (user, reason, TOTP/approval token) kept for 12 months.
- Private deployment considerations: you asked whether Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration and whether keys can be customer-managed.

Attached two artifacts I promised on the call: a draft support-access playbook and the privacy questionnaire you started. See attachments: support-access-playbook-v0.1.pdf, acadia_privacy_qs.xlsx.

Proposed immediate next steps (we can pick dates in the thread):
1) Redwood: produce a roles-to-permissions mapping template for Acadia's environments (who is Support, SRE, Incident Commander) — owner: Marissa.
2) Acadia: share the list of team emails that should be allowed JIT access and a sample escalation contact — owner: Emma.
3) Redwood: confirm KMS/HSM options and whether customer key import is supported in Private — owner: Ben.
4) Schedule an internal tech deep-dive to walk through the break-glass runbook and log evidence sample — propose next Tue/Wed.

If that aligns, we'll convert this into a mutual action plan by end of week with owners and dates.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

On Fri, Apr 16, 2027 at 10:02 AM Emma Park <emma.park@acadiahealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sean — appreciated the overview. We need the role mapping template sooner rather than later. One clarifying Q: in emergency scenarios our SOC wants the ability to request temporary access to de-identified raw logs for triage; can we confirm what level of masking/redaction Redwood can do before logs are delivered to our S3?
> 
> Also, on the KMS piece, is Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) available for Private deployments or only hosted? Tom and I will flag with our security architect.
> 
> Best,
> Emma

From: Emma Park <emma.park@acadiahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@acadiahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T17:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Operationalizing support access & break-glass — Acadia Health follow-up

Sean — thanks for the summary and the attachments. A couple of additional notes from our security team:

- Redaction rules: we can accept redacted logs for initial triage, but for full forensic exercises we may need time-limited access to less-redacted entries. That should still be guarded by the JIT + approval flow.
- Proof of audit: can you provide a sample audit record that shows the approval chain (requestor, approver, timestamp, reason)? Our SOC will want to validate format.
- Audit retention: 12 months is fine for now but we'll confirm with legal.

We'll gather our list of escalation contacts and the first-pass team list (expected by EOD Monday). Re: BYOK — we'll wait for Ben's note.

Emma Park
Senior Security Engineer, Acadia Health
emma.park@acadiahealth.com | +1 (919) 555-0242

On Fri, Apr 16, 2027 at 12:02 PM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Great — looking forward to the SOC feedback.
>

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-17T13:07:00Z
Subject: Internal: Acadia action plan & deliverables (draft)

Team —

Following Emma's clarifications, here's a draft mutual action plan I can own and circulate to Acadia once we align internally. Please flag edits inline.

MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (draft)
- Owner: Marissa Cole (RWD) — create final MAP and circulate by 2027-04-20.
- Deliverable A (2027-04-22): Roles-to-permissions mapping template. Fields: Role name, Redwood service ACLs, allowed JIT scopes, max session duration, approver group.
- Deliverable B (2027-04-23): Sample audit record export (JSON + human-readable). Contains: request_id, requester, approver, approval_token, timestamp, reason, affected_resources.
- Deliverable C (2027-04-25): Support break-glass runbook (steps, contacts, escalation matrix, rollback checklist).
- Deliverable D (by 2027-04-27): KMS/HSM options doc + steps for customer key import (if supported) and recommended architecture for Private deployments.

Internal asks for Ben/Infra team: confirm BYOK semantics and whether import with HSM wrapping is supported for on-prem and VPC (Ben, can you validate and attach any vendor docs?).

Marissa will draft the policy language for JIT approval TTL and default RBAC least-privilege rules; Sean — please confirm if we want to propose a 15-minute default session or 1 hour for emergency sessions. Emma asked for short-lived by default but we should check typical customer needs.

I'll create a HubSpot task and attach the artifacts to the shared Drive folder.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0139

On Sat, Apr 17, 2027 at 08:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Adding a quick note: I will take point on the KMS/HSM confirmation and produce Deliverable D. Ben will also collect SOC2 evidence snippets (audit schema examples) and upload to the Drive link Marissa creates. Expect a short write-up by Monday lunchtime.
>

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: Acadia action plan & deliverables (draft)

Got it — I'll own the KMS/HSM write-up and the SOC2 evidence pack. Quick confirmations:

- BYOK: Private supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration; we support key import and HSM wrapping for on-prem appliance installs. For VPC-hosted Private we can offer AWS KMS BYOK flow or a bring-your-HSM option depending on the deployment. I'll enumerate exact limitations in the doc.
- Audit sample: I'll attach a redacted JSON sample showing request and approval metadata.

I will upload both artifacts to the Drive folder and cc Emma when the KMS doc is ready.

Ben Carter
Security Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0187
